title: Stakeholder map, meeting plan and discovery guide
story: As the candidate I need a two-page stakeholder map and a discovery guide for the CTO and the Head of Digital Transformation so that I open the 40 minutes with the right questions, adapt the flow to what I hear, and equip the champion to carry the case to the people who are not in the room.
acceptance: strategy/stakeholder-map.md opens with a three-line summary (objective, the ask, the single biggest risk to the meeting). Everything before the "## Appendix" heading fits two pages: running  awk '/^## Appendix/{exit} {print}' strategy/stakeholder-map.md | wc -w  prints 1200 or fewer (about two printed pages; table pipes inflate the count), and an "## Appendix" heading exists.

For each of the CTO and the Head of Digital Transformation the body gives: goals, fears, what they must hear (one sentence in the candidate's voice), the proof they need, how to engage them in the room, and at least 3 signals to watch for, each with a planned response. Persona traits trace to brief/facts.json; anything else is labelled "Assumption:" or phrased as typical for executives in regulated finance.

An absent-stakeholders table covers CISO, risk and compliance, model risk, engineering managers, procurement and finance. Each row has: likely concern (typical, not a FinTechCo fact), what they will ask the champion, the leave-behind that answers it by deliverable id (D5 ROI model, D6 evaluation plan, D7 security brief, D8 follow-up kit) and our offer to help. A short "champion kit" list says what the Head of Digital Transformation carries away to sell internally.

Exactly three win themes: grep -c '^### Win theme' strategy/stakeholder-map.md prints 3. Each ties to a FinTechCo priority from brief/facts.json (team productivity, shipping new products) or to safe control, and names its proof as a [CLM-?: ...] placeholder.

Risks to the meeting: grep -c '^| R-' strategy/stakeholder-map.md prints 6 or more. Each row has a trigger, a mitigation and the related ADR-005 checkpoint or cut (for example 0:12 demo start, 0:26 demo end, 0:37 wrap).

The ask section restates ADR-005 without changing its substance: CTO opens a security and compliance review (we send the review package; working session with their security team within a week); Head of Digital Transformation names a pilot cohort across all three teams and a metrics owner to capture baselines; together they set a pilot kickoff date; success means both agree and the CTO's top concern is named and has an owner.

strategy/discovery.md has: a 30-second "what we heard" recap using only brief/facts.json facts; one primary opening question for the CTO and one for the Head of Digital Transformation, written as spoken lines with an estimated speaking time (~140 wpm) so both fit the 3-minute Open segment; at least 3 follow-ups per attendee, each with a "why we ask"; and at least 6 deeper questions reserved for the security working session or follow-up call.

strategy/discovery.md has a flow-adjustment table: grep -c '^| F-' strategy/discovery.md prints 8 or more. Each row maps "if we hear X" to the ADR-005 segments to expand, cut or reorder, the minutes added or saved, and the effect on the 0:12, 0:26 and 0:37 checkpoints; net plan stays within 40 minutes with wrap-up starting by 0:37. A default flow for "just start presenting" (no discovery time) is included, and a 3-line note-taking template feeds the wrap-up.

Claims rule (ADR-006): every external fact carries a specific [CLM-?: what to source] placeholder; a [CLM-###] id appears only if it already exists in research/claims/*.json as verified or partial. Running  node org/contracts/validate.mjs | grep -E 'FAIL.*strategy/(stakeholder-map|discovery)' || echo clean  prints clean.

Nothing is invented about FinTechCo beyond brief/facts.json (no existing tools, regulators, vendors, org names or budgets stated as fact); no real people, secrets or Anthropic brand assets; only this ticket's two paths were changed; a handoff listing unresolved placeholders is posted to hub strategy.
brief:
Audience: the candidate (a principal architect) reading this the night before and glancing at it in the room. Executives read the first line, so lead with the point. Stance per ADR-005: advisor, not seller. The Head of Digital Transformation is also someone you arm to sell internally after you leave (REQ-16).

stakeholder-map.md. First three lines: objective, the ask, biggest risk. Then a body of two pages at most, then "## Appendix" for depth (persona notes, full risk register, per-stakeholder detail). Body order: (1) the two attendees: goals, fears, what they must hear, proof needed, how to engage in the room (tone, who to address first, where to hand over control), signals to watch with a response each (for example the CTO raises security before 0:26: answer in 20 seconds only if it blocks, otherwise park it and promise the 0:26 segment). (2) Absent-stakeholders table plus champion kit. (3) Three "### Win theme n" headings. (4) Risk table with ids R-01, R-02, ... (5) The ask, per ADR-005.

discovery.md. 30-second "what we heard" recap from facts.json only (productivity, shipping products, one tool within months, no agentic tools today, evaluating alongside others). One opening question per attendee as a spoken line with its speaking time. At least 3 follow-ups each with "why we ask". At least 6 deeper security-session questions. Then "## Flow adjustments", a table with ids F-01, F-02, ...: "If we hear..." -> expand, cut or reorder -> minutes delta -> checkpoint effect. Use ADR-005 segment names and section numbers (Deck sections 1 to 8); slide numbers do not exist before G1. End with the note-taking template.

Pitfalls: FinTechCo is fictional; for anything not in facts.json write "executives in regulated finance often..." or label it "Assumption:". Your ticket owns no claims shard, so use [CLM-?: precise thing to source], for example [CLM-?: named regulated-industry Claude Code adopters, exactly as published]. Do not wait for or cite sibling tickets' files (objection-handling, use-cases); refer to them by name only. No disparagement of competitors, no superlatives.
